new_symbol_range_suggestions.protonated_group_hill_coefficient: positive, typically 1/2 to 2; equal to 1 recovers the ideal independent titration limit

derivation_notes: The parent assumes unit-slope Henderson-Hasselbalch protonation for each required catalytic ionization. Here the protonated-required occupancy factor is given an effective Hill-type steepness so local electrostatic coupling or unresolved microstate averaging can sharpen or broaden the acidic flank while preserving static equilibrium and the same ionic-strength-shifted pKa center.
change_summary: The required-protonated titration step no longer has fixed unit steepness. This refines the pH-response law by changing flank curvature and peak sharpness at fixed ionic strength without adding inputs or states.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Each catalytic ionization is represented by an ideal two-state unit-slope titration curve.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Apparent nonideal protonation steepness from local electrostatic coupling, microstate heterogeneity, or rapid unresolved conformational averaging
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when protonated_group_hill_coefficient = 1.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed ionic_strength, the competent-state occupancy is the product of two independent Henderson-Hasselbalch factors, so log10(k_app) has a single symmetric bell-like pH window determined only by two effective pKa values, with any intrinsic competent-state pH effect entering only as a local linear tilt around the window center.
response_change.child_relation: Retain the same two-group occupancy logic but relax the idealized assumption that each protonation step is perfectly noncooperative. Model one or both acid-base transitions with an effective Hill-type steepness, allowing the pH window flanks to become sharper or broader than the parent predicts while preserving a single activity window.
response_change.observable_effect: Across pH scans at different fixed ionic_strength values, the rise and fall of activity around the window can show systematically altered flank steepness and peak sharpness that cannot be matched by merely shifting the pKa values or applying one shared turnover tilt.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when pH is sampled sufficiently across both acidic and basic flanks of the activity window, especially when ionic_strength is high enough for local electrostatic restructuring to matter but still within the non-denaturing buffered regime; the effect is strongest when deviations from ideal unit-slope protonation curves exceed experimental noise.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, modest deviations appear as slightly too-sharp or too-broad shoulders near the peak; in holdout, the same nonideal steepness yields clearer mismatch on farther flanks or at ionic_strength values where electrostatic coupling strengthens the apparent cooperativity.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the effective protonation steepness returns to the ideal independent value of 1 for the relaxed transition(s), or when data are restricted to a narrow pH region near the peak where altered flank steepness is weakly expressed.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: nonideal acid-base titration steepness in the protonated-required catalytic group
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Apparent nonideal protonation steepness from local electrostatic coupling, microstate heterogeneity, or rapid unresolved conformational averaging can make the occupancy of the catalytically competent protonation pattern vary with pH more sharply or more gradually than the ideal independent form.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the new parameter changes the coefficient of the existing pH-displacement term inside an occupancy exponent, altering the curvature of the scored pH-to-k_app mapping rather than merely shifting peak position or scaling height.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Protonation equilibrates before activity is measured, and each catalytic ionization is represented by an ideal two-state unit-slope titration curve.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Protonation still equilibrates before measurement, but the required-protonated group's titration can have nonideal Hill-type steepness while remaining a single static equilibrium transition.

evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Set protonated_group_hill_coefficient = 1 to recover the parent exactly.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Vary pH while holding ionic_strength fixed for each scan, then compare scans across ionic_strength. The child preserves the same ionic-strength-dependent pKa shifts and turnover tilt but allows the acidic-side flank and peak sharpness of the activity window to be systematically sharper or broader than the parent's enforced unit-slope occupancy law.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set can shift the effective pKa values, alter overall height, and add one ionic-strength-activated linear turnover tilt, but it still enforces unit-slope occupancy flanks on both sides of the activity window. Therefore it cannot reproduce persistent pH-window curvature differences across scans that require non-unit titration steepness rather than mere peak relocation or rescaling.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when pH is sampled sufficiently across both acidic and basic flanks of the activity window, especially when ionic_strength is high enough for local electrostatic restructuring to matter but still within the non-denaturing buffered regime; the effect is strongest when deviations from ideal unit-slope protonation curves exceed experimental noise.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, modest deviations appear as slightly too-sharp or too-broad shoulders near the peak; in holdout, the same nonideal steepness yields clearer mismatch on farther flanks or at ionic_strength values where electrostatic coupling strengthens the apparent cooperativity.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the effective protonation steepness returns to the ideal independent value of 1 for the relaxed transition(s), or when data are restricted to a narrow pH region near the peak where altered flank steepness is weakly expressed.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes each required protonation equilibrium follows an ideal independent Henderson-Hasselbalch transition with fixed unit steepness, which can be too restrictive for active sites where nearby charges and solvent reorganization broaden or sharpen the pH response.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Protonation equilibrates before activity is measured, and each catalytic ionization is represented by an ideal two-state unit-slope titration curve.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Apparent nonideal protonation steepness from local electrostatic coupling, microstate heterogeneity, or rapid unresolved conformational averaging can make the occupancy of the catalytically competent protonation pattern vary with pH more sharply or more gradually than the ideal independent form.
evolution_plan.rationale: The parent already includes ionic-strength-dependent pKa shifts and an ionic-strength-activated intrinsic-turnover tilt, so a natural remaining gap is not another omitted process but the idealized shape of the protonation transitions themselves. Vary pH while holding ionic_strength fixed for each scan, then compare scans across ionic_strength. The parent can move the peak and alter overall height or local skew through the turnover factor, but with one shared parameter set it still enforces unit-slope occupancy flanks on both sides of the activity window. A child that allows nonideal steepness changes the target mapping itself: the acidic and/or basic shoulders gain different curvature and peak sharpness even after refitting all existing parent parameters. This is scientifically admissible in equilibrated, non-denaturing buffered measurements because local electrostatic coupling and unresolved microheterogeneity can distort apparent titration steepness without violating static equilibrium assumptions. The contrast is observable only when pH coverage includes the flanks; if measurements are confined near the peak, the refinement may be weakly identifiable.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Make the coefficient of an existing process depend on a declared quantity.

scenario_text: Measure the apparent catalytic activity of an enzyme across buffered pH conditions at fixed, saturating substrate abundance. Catalysis requires one enzyme group to be protonated and another to be deprotonated, creating a restricted pH window in which the catalytically competent microstate is abundant. Each pH condition is sampled independently after equilibration, and irreversible protein damage is excluded from the baseline response.
